defects: Restricts the scalar field to ℝ only, whereas the gold statement works over any RCLike 𝕜 (including ℂ) — a real loss of generality.

Adds an un-stated hypothesis that the codomain F has the same finite dimension n as the domain E (forced by requiring a Basis (Fin n) ℝ F). The gold statement only requires the domain U to be finite-dimensional; V (the codomain) can be infinite-dimensional or of strictly larger finite dimension, so a general isometric embedding into a bigger/infinite space is excluded from the produced statement.

Replaces the citation of the actual Mathlib `LinearMap.normDet` (the intended, basis-independent norm-determinant) with an ad hoc matrix-determinant formula tied to a specific arbitrary pair of orthonormal bases; this only coincides with the general theorem in the special case dim E = dim F, so it is not a faithful restatement of the gold proposition.

The arguments to `LinearMap.toMatrix` appear swapped: Mathlib's convention is `toMatrix (domainBasis) (codomainBasis)`, but the statement calls `LinearMap.toMatrix b_F b_E ↑f` with f : E →ₗ[ℝ] F, which requires the domain/codomain bases in the order (b_E, b_F); as written this is a type mismatch and the statement likely fails to elaborate.
